correctness.rationale: Starting from the source SPS formula, the dimensionless map is derived exactly. For \(0<q<2\), both branches strictly decrease magnitude; cap activity is invariant once reached; perpetual uncapped motion would force a limiting magnitude simultaneously above \(\sqrt{2/3}\) and equal to it, a contradiction. For \(q\ge2\), direct substitution at \(x_\star=\sqrt{2c/(3a)}\) gives normalized step \(2\), hence an exact sign-flip two-cycle. Substitution into the source stability-index formula gives \(\frac{4c}{3}(1-1/q)\). The proof covers branch equality at \(q=2\), all \(a,c>0\), all \(\alpha>0\), and declares the zero-gradient minimizer fixed. Numerical replay checks but does not replace these universal arguments.

value.rationale: The source explicitly makes lower-bound estimation error a determinant of SPS stability, so the simplest strongly convex one-sample quadratic with a strict valid lower-bound error is a motivated boundary case rather than an arbitrary slice. The result supplies a sharp iff threshold, a natural exact cycle, and the objective scale \(c/3\), showing concretely that bounded stability-index behavior can coexist with nonconvergent iterates. This clarifies the interpretation of a new stability framework without claiming a general algorithmic lower bound.
